log: Working out who would actually buy this
Discovering candidates and exact source URLs (stage 1 of 2)
Fetching up to 10 exact URLs; validating against at most 48,000 characters
Evaluating candidates against 9 fetched pages (stage 2 of 2)

Coverage gaps and failures. (1) Quotes in this map come from search-result summaries, not from fetched pages; every one needs confirming against the source URL before use in copy, and the publisher-sourced statistics I saw (percentage of coordinator time on admin, minutes to schedule an interview, candidate ghosting rates) are unverified vendor-blog numbers that I have deliberately kept out of the pains and definitions. (2) Direct buyer voice was the main failure. Four targeted attempts at Reddit and community threads (r/sales inbound routing, r/consulting paid discovery calls, booker-side privacy discomfort, teams cancelling paid schedulers for free Google appointment schedules) returned comparison articles and vendor pages instead of threads — the search layer appears to favour SEO content over forum posts for these phrasings. Named-forum searching (community.calendly.com, Indie Hackers, G2 reviewer text) should be run directly on those domains. (3) No named organisation is on record as a SavvyCal customer in anything I found beyond the vendor's own testimonials already in the brief, so no candidate here carries a purchase example. (4) The single most important unknown is unresolved: what a recipient has to do to overlay their calendar, what is stored, and how many recipients actually do it. Without that, the overlay-led pitch rests entirely on sender-side opinion. (5) Scope was unspecified, so I set no geographic boundary and searched in English only; non-English demand is unexamined. (6) Two plausible segments were dropped for want of evidence: podcast hosts booking guests (Calendly and Acuity dominate the published workflows and I found no host complaint that SavvyCal specifically answers) and executive assistants using delegated access (the delegation pain is well documented in travel and Outlook contexts, but nothing tied it to scheduling-link products). (7) Population counts are unknown throughout; no directory I saw demonstrates intent, only existence.
6 audience(s) mapped; 0 worth exploring first. Commercial priority is a hypothesis, not a response-rate forecast.
